method: Independent manual sequential inspection of all108 final runtime cells, all nine seams with last3/first3 native-size neighbor sheets, and separate native six-cell turn-exit and raised-arm strips. Full224x243 GIF/WebP assembled from the same final runtime pixels and timing; no claim of fluency based only on hashes, frame count or fps.

seams.observation: Head and outfit stay consistent. Entry ends with crossed feet and the next first frame resets to parallel feet. The next two frames begin crossing again. A small stance reset remains, without a size or floor pop.
Clasped-hands frontal body and face agree. Parallel feet become a crossed ankle stance at the next first frame. Head crown stays close and the step is smaller than a body-height discontinuity.
Leaning/crossed stance straightens into the front neutral with both shoes parallel. Head tilt, skirt/ponytail width and arm linework change slightly across the cut; identity remains stable.

Both front clasped-hands poses and parallel feet agree. The head straightens slightly and the hair/skirt silhouette changes with a few-pixel crown difference. There is no conspicuous whole-character scale change.

Segment04/11 exits the turn as a screen-right three-quarter face with extended arms; segment05/00 goes back to a screen-right profile and clasped hands, then segment05/01–02 returns to the front. This is a visible brief yaw back-step at the turn exit rather than a fully monotonic turn continuation. Bbox heights stay close, so it is a pose/direction step, not a scale pop.

Closed-eye smile, screen-left raised arm, screen-right lifted leg and costume remain correct across the cut. The raised arm shifts from a steeper angle to a diagonal and the lifted shoe becomes more horizontal/outward in the next cell. This is a visible one-cell hand/foot position step, with no left/right leg exchange or head-height collapse.

Same open-eye face, raised screen-left arm and outward screen-right leg continue into the return family. Return01 then lowers that arm and draws the lifted foot inward in actual successive poses. Minor head tilt/frill/ponytail linework changes remain.

Both shoes are grounded and parallel at the boundary. The screen-left arm begins Return02 a little higher than the final Return01 arm, then lowers to neutral. Face size and ground plane remain consistent.

Both cells are neutral front standing with matching head/body height: solid194/193px, crownY7/8. There is no former shortened return figure or large vertical pop. The ponytail/hair and skirt silhouette is wider in the return cell (solid140px versus121px in entry), and foot spacing/facial shading differ slightly between independent drawings. Not a pixel-identical neutral bookend.

remaining_visible_pose_steps: Segment04/11→segment05/00 temporarily returns from right three-quarter face to right profile before finishing the turn.
Segment05/11→segment06-seam/00 changes raised-arm and outward-foot angles in one cell.
remaining_minor: Other early stage transitions have slight stance/head-tilt or linework changes.
Loop neutral has wider ponytail/skirt silhouette and slightly different foot spacing/shading.
overall: All108 cells are complete and maintain Cecilia identity and the cafe maid costume. The three repaired continuation/return segments preserve the same outward screen-right foot and comparable head/body scale, with actual progressive arm lowering and leg recovery. No major scale collapse, blank actor or foot-phase swap is seen. The two visible pose steps above remain, so this review accepts the assets as usable but does not call the loop perfectly seamless.

technical_support.registration_note: BBox bottom203 is the exclusive bound and corresponds to last nontransparent pixel y202. Final runtime cells only were reviewed. Sources, actor scale, runtime assets and parent manifest were not changed.

scope_limit: Rendered continuity, character identity and clothing only; no fresh official-OP timecode/choreography audit. The optional visible-step polish must use genuinely matching drawn pose endpoints, not per-character raster scaling.
